title: Man. Post. Cap. II: Placeus — three reasons joined; French par consequent; Nero / Matt–Luke
pass_a_gloss: PLAC. First he attributes to me an argumentation that is not mine. For this, as I said, I joined with the prior, so that from those two I might gather a third, in which the reason of imputation chiefly consists. Which can be clear from that third reason which he professes to have gathered from my letters in this same ch. 2 section x pp. 35-36. For in it those three are coupled which he here divided so that a double change can be noted. First for hereditary corruption he put a vice not existing in us. Then he omitted the causal conjunction therefore, so, or the like, answering in that place to the French words par consequent which I had used in that letter, and from which it appears I seek the reason of imputation from habitual consent to that sin included in hereditary corruption: and that I gather this consent from this, that that corruption is nothing else than the habitual depravity of that first actual sin, which it left in Adam's soul, and which propagated into us inclines us to like sin. For the rest I do not know whether even here he seems to dispute against the Lord's own words in Matt. 23:34 and Luke 11:50-51. For what is it, why, for example, Nero's cruel deeds could not somehow be imputed to one equally cruel and savage in mind, seeing that it does not stand by his will that he not perpetrate the same, equally cruel namely?
pass_b_english: Placeus: First he pins on me an argument that is not mine. As I said, I joined this with the prior point so that from those two I could draw a third, where the reason for imputation chiefly sits. That is plain from the third reason he says he gathered from my letters in this same chapter 2 section x, pp. 35-36. There those three points are linked; here he split them so you can mark a double change. First, for hereditary corruption he put a vice that does not exist in us. Next he dropped the causal link—'therefore,' 'so,' or the like—matching the French par consequent I had used in that letter, from which it is clear I take the reason of imputation from habitual consent to that sin as included in hereditary corruption, and that I gather this consent because that corruption is nothing but the habitual depravity of that first actual sin, which it left in Adam's soul and which, propagated into us, inclines us to like sin. I am not sure he is not also arguing here against the Lord's own words in Matthew 23:34 and Luke 11:50-51. Why, for example, could Nero's cruel deeds not somehow be charged to someone equally cruel and savage in mind, when it is not by his will that he fails to do the same—being equally cruel?
source_text: PLAC. Primo tribuit mihi argumentationem non meam. Hoc enim, ut dixi, conjunxi cum superiori, ut ex duobus illis tertium colligerem, in quo ratio imputationis potissimum consistit. Id quod ex tertia illa ratione, quam ex literis meis se collegisse profitetur hoc eodem cap. 2. § x. pag. 35. 36. liquere potest. In ea enim copulantur ista tria quae hoc loco divisit sic ut duplex mutatio notari possit. Primo enim pro corruptione haereditaria reposuit vitium in nobis inexsistens. Deinde omisit conjunctionem causalem propterea, adeo, aut similem, respondentem eo loco vocibus gallicis par consequent, quibus in illa epistola usus fueram, & ex quibus apparet, rationem imputationis me petere a consensu habituali ad illud peccatum in corruptione haereditaria incluso: hunc autem consensum ex eo colligere, quod illa corruptio nihil aliud est quam primi illius peccati actualis pravitas habitualis, quam in Adami anima reliquit, & quae in nos propagata nos ad simile peccatum inclinat. Caeterum nescio annon etiam hoc loco adversus ipsius Domini verba disputare videatur, quae habentur Matth. 23. 34. & Luc. xi. 50. 51. Quid est enim, cur, exempli causa, non possint aliquomodo crudelia facinora Neronis ei, qui sit animo aeque crudeli & immani, imputari, quandoquidem quominus eadem perpetret per ejus voluntatem non stat, aeque videlicet crudelem?

choices.choice: Keep split of three reasons, French par consequent, Matt 23:34 / Luke 11:50-51 Nero parallel
choices.why: Placeus restores joined ratio of imputation
